clue.text: Try again — that's the opposite of how this answer goes!

definitions.text: Try again — that's the opposite of how this answer goes!

parts.words: Try again — that's the opposite of how this answer goes!
parts.note: starting afresh means returning to the beginning; this light starts in the very first square of the grid and runs forward, the opposite of going back to it

explanation.surface: An exasperated instruction to have another go, with a joke about the puzzle itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is positional: this is 1-across, so the answer begins in the grid's first square and travels away from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means returning to the starting point after a failed attempt, so trying again from scratch.

clue.text: Business details underwear mountains

parts.note: bras are items of women's underwear
mountains of something are stacks of it, great heaps

explanation.surface: A headline about an absurd surplus of lingerie in a company's accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting down to the idiom means dealing with the basic practical facts of a matter.

clue.text: Tank's run out — ring around for relative skilled with tools?

indicators.note: around says the bell-ringing word encloses the rest

parts.note: to ring a bell is to chime

indicators.note: run out says the R is taken out of the tank word

parts.note: a Panzer is a German tank
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A soldier reporting that the tank has run dry and must call for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' and 'around' are the indicators. The question mark flags a playful definition: apes are our evolutionary relatives and famous tool users.
explanation.definitionFit: This great ape is a close kin of humans and is known for using sticks and stones as implements.

clue.text: 'Wet' beer shop — that drunken establishment

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters stagger about into a new order

explanation.surface: A sneer at a pub where weak beer is served and the patrons are sozzled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Establishment' looks like the pub; it is the ruling class.
explanation.definitionFit: The Establishment is the group holding authority in society, the people in charge.

clue.text: Say Glaswegian clubs kicked out drunk

indicators.note: kicked out says the clubs letter is ejected from the nationality word

parts.note: someone from Glasgow is, for instance (hence 'Say'), Scottish
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A drunken Glaswegian being thrown out of nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking C from SCOTTISH leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes someone fuddled by alcohol, like a sot or habitual drinker.

clue.text: Dull college class

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A complaint about a boring university seminar.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unvarying and monotonous, the same throughout, is dull.

clue.text: Gain land, weirdly knackered but up for it

indicators.note: knackered means broken or worn out, so the letters are wrecked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone exhausted from strangely acquiring property yet still keen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weirdly' looks like the anagram signal but it is fodder; 'knackered' (British slang for exhausted or broken) does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe being eager and prepared to take part.

clue.text: 'Five Go Off To Be Sick'? Leave it out!

indicators.note: go off says the numeral departs from the word for being sick

parts.note: to be sick is to vomit
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: An Enid Blyton parody title, 'Five Go Off To Be Sick', met with a groan.
explanation.walkthrough: The Famous Five books by Enid Blyton had titles like 'Five Go Off to Camp'; here the Five leave VOMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude or skip something is to leave it out; the exclamation also fits the groan.

clue.text: Moneyed gentleman holding advantage

indicators.note: holding says the two words contain the letters within them

explanation.surface: A wealthy man has the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an advantage over a rival is having a slight lead on them.

clue.text: Take a spin on street that's most lifeless

parts.note: a spin in a car is a ride

explanation.surface: A suggestion to go for a drive down the dullest road around.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of dry, it means most barren, dull or devoid of life.

clue.text: One's getting on in x-ray department

parts.note: one is, said in the first person, gives I'M
getting on in years means growing old

explanation.surface: An older person admitting their age while visiting the hospital radiology unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The hospital unit doing scans and radiography is often named for this process of producing pictures of the body.

clue.text: With no backing, presume Morph's Conservative? You know where you can stick that!

definitions.text: You know where you can stick that!

indicators.note: no backing says the end of the word is dropped

parts.note: to presume is to suppose
the setter Morph refers to himself as I
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A rude retort to someone who assumes the setter votes Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no backing' removes the final letter. Setters often refer to themselves as I, so 'Morph's' is I's.
explanation.definitionFit: The rude retort tells someone to insert something up their rear, where this medicine is placed.

clue.text: Fouled goal hero, collecting yellow, not holding back verbally!

definitions.note: a phrase describing a noun condition: an unstoppable flow of words

indicators.note: collecting says the jumbled letters take in the colour word
fouled suggests the letters are messed up into a new order

parts.note: the clue words taken as written
or is the heraldic term for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: A footballer who scored but got booked for a foul, then ranted at the referee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fouled' makes LOGRHOEA, and 'collecting' puts OR inside it; OR as yellow comes from heraldry, where it means gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term names excessive, uncontrollable talkativeness, a torrent of speech.

clue.text: Young women from house of horror may be leading lights in cinema

definitions.text: Young women from house of horror
definitions.meaning: a pun: Edgar Allan Poe's horror tale is The Fall of the House of Usher, and -ette makes a young female version
cinema attendants who show patrons to their seats with a torch

explanation.surface: Girls fleeing a haunted house might later work at the pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: These were women employed in cinemas to guide people to seats by torchlight, so literally lights that lead.

clue.text: Young woman touring Vienna heading off

indicators.note: touring suggests the letters travel around into a new order
heading off says the first letter is removed

explanation.surface: A girl on a sightseeing trip around the Austrian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Vienna loses V, leaving IENNA, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, as with the orphan in the musical, stands for a young woman.

clue.text: Giant antelope heading back over to probe rotting matter

indicators.note: to probe says the pieces push into the soil word

parts.note: humus is decomposed plant matter in soil

indicators.note: heading back says the animal word is turned round

parts.note: a gnu is a kind of antelope
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A huge antelope turning to sniff at decaying vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading back' makes UNG; 'to probe' sends it, with O, into the soil word. O for over is a cricket convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang adjective means enormous, as big as a giant.

clue.text: With financial support, boy volunteers to back nags

parts.note: one's keep is the cost of food and lodging, financial support
a son is a boy

indicators.note: to back says the volunteers' letters are turned round

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A funded boy and helpers putting money on horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nags' looks like horses to bet on; it is the verb, to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who nags pesters persistently, repeatedly urging another person.

clue.text: Nirvana hit that may be put out on a platter?

definitions.text: that may be put out on a platter?
definitions.note: a definition by example: a dish one might serve

indicators.note: hit suggests the letters are struck and knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A Nirvana hit record, a platter being slang for a vinyl disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Platter' suggests a record for the band; it is a serving dish.
explanation.definitionFit: This French lamb stew with vegetables is a dish served up at table.

clue.text: Hard to support narcissistic politician with ego in victory

indicators.note: in a down light, to support means to go beneath the rest
in says the self letter goes inside the politician

parts.note: Donald Trump, the US politician noted for self-regard
the ego is the self, I
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Struggling to back a vain politician whose ego swells in victory.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great success or win.

clue.text: Rubbish you and I have committed to paper

indicators.note: have says the pair holds the nonsense word

parts.note: you and I together are we
rot is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: A rueful admission that we have written nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To commit words to paper is to have written them down.

clue.text: Eight rave boisterously around city to do this?

definitions.text: Eight rave boisterously around city to do this?

indicators.note: around says the jumbled letters surround the city
boisterously suggests the letters romp about into a new order

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Eight friends partying wildly through a city, which is exactly what the answer means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boisterously' makes HAVEITRGE, and 'around' wraps it round LA. Read whole, the clue also describes raving rowdily round town.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang idiom means to party hard and enjoy oneself extravagantly.

clue.text: Legislation plays a part

definitions.meaning: ... of Parliament are pieces of legislation
a performer who plays a part on stage performs

explanation.surface: Lawmaking has a role to play.
explanation.definitionFit: Laws passed by Parliament carry this name; it also means performs a role.

clue.text: Turned up a bit of information

indicators.note: in a down light, turned up means read from the bottom upward

parts.note: a tad is a small bit

explanation.surface: Someone found a scrap of information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of information' looks like a single datum; 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts and figures collected for reference or analysis are information.

clue.text: Vessel that may be covered by another, e.g. schooner

definitions.meaning: a ship trading along the shore, a vessel

definitions.text: that may be covered by another, e.g. schooner
definitions.meaning: a drinks mat lies under a glass; a schooner is a large sherry or beer glass, itself another vessel

explanation.surface: A sailing ship eclipsed by another type of ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Schooner' suggests a sailing ship, but here it is a drinking glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small shipping boat and the mat a drink is set down on.

clue.text: Man loudly open about sexuality in publicity blitz

indicators.note: loudly says the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a man is male
someone who is out is open about being gay

explanation.surface: A man coming out publicly as part of a media campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass mailing of promotional material is a publicity campaign.

clue.text: Almost nude, caught in transgression, gets rash about hidden danger

indicators.note: caught in says the trimmed word is held within the wrongdoing

parts.note: a transgression is a sin

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is lost

parts.note: nude means naked

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A streaker caught in the act breaks out in a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost', 'caught in' and 'about' are the indicators. 'Rash' looks like a skin complaint, but with 'gets' it is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a treacherous person or concealed threat, like a viper lurking unseen.
